narrative.overview: A landscape photo carries the screen; a frosted instrument panel of measurements sits on it; below it a light, dense register answers whether everything fits. Quiet by default, loud only when a decision is needed. Since the last recording, the language was consolidated into one token layer (ui/kit.css) and painted across all 33 wireframe pages / 20 screens, extending the vocabulary with hub short-hero screens, the card-photo pattern reused for the Guide/Safety article grid, the avatar row, and the avalanche-danger scale.
keyCharacteristics: Photo-led hero with a frosted instrument panel
One action colour, one live-state colour
Large radii on containers, flat rows
Tektur digits, Wix Madefor Display language
A short hero photo carries the h1 directly on hub screens with no head block (Guide, Safety)

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Blue only on things that are pressed or actionable.

rules.name: The Word First Rule
rules.body: No state carried by colour alone — including the avalanche scale, read by its word, never by yellow alone.

rules.name: The Closed Palette Rule
rules.body: A colour not listed in ui/kit.css's :root is a defect.

rules.name: The Floor Rule
rules.body: Text 12px+; 10px only for the tab bar, badge, day-chain node number and uppercase measurement label.

rules.name: The Number First Rule
rules.body: A unit is never the size of its number.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards and lists never cast shadows.

dos: Do put the three key measurements on the photo in the instrument panel
Do print author and licence on every photo and ©Kartverket on every map
Do keep white text on photos on glass no lighter than rgba(15,17,19,.45), or behind the text shadow where a glass chip would be too heavy
Do reuse .card-photo for any future photo-led grid rather than inventing a new card shape
donts: Don't use blue for anything that isn't pressed or actionable
Don't use a Unicode glyph as an icon
Don't reuse the official difficulty grading's colours (green/blue/red/black) for anything else in the product
Don't add a kicker/eyebrow label — none of the 20 screens use one, and none is evidenced in ui/kit.css
